portraits.prompt: A woman of about fifty, calm and encouraging drill instructor of the coastal Westbund army, short grey-streaked hair, kind but firm eyes, clean pale-blue and white uniform with a small headset. Cool blue accent light.

Dr. Elin Voss, early forties, chief strategist of the coastal Westbund, composed and tired, dark hair tied back, high-collared slate-blue coat with silver insignia, thin glasses pushed up, quiet resolve under heavy burden. Cool teal and white light.

Major Kai Laurent called Falke, mid-thirties fighter pilot, cocky half-smile, tousled hair, stubble, flight jacket patched from salvaged parts, goggles on forehead, oil smudge on cheek. Warm cockpit amber light with cool blue fill.

Sergeant Mira Tanaka called Glas, early thirties Japanese-descent sniper, silent and watchful, cropped black hair, cold steady eyes, light grey-blue armor with a cloth scarf, faint scar on chin. Pale blue light, shallow shadows.

ORAKEL, an artificial intelligence shown as a calm abstract face of cyan light: a luminous ring-shaped lens or eye floating in darkness, faint geometric human face outlined in glowing lines, serene and uncanny. Cyan and white glow on black.

Dr. Yusuf Brandt, fifty-year-old Middle Eastern prism researcher, nervous and brilliant, round glasses, rumpled lab coat over sweater, grey-flecked beard, ink on fingers, curious wide eyes. Soft blue screen light.

Henrik Aldane, sixty-year-old council president of the Westbund, smooth authoritative statesman, silver hair combed back, immaculate dark formal coat with a council chain, calm confident expression that hides something. Cold white light.

Lena Voss, early forties, Elin's sister and fighter of the Shadow Front, warm but hardened face, wavy dark hair with ash in it, patched earth-colored hooded cloak, weary eyes full of love and sorrow. Warm low firelight with violet shadow.
Mother Karga, ancient highland woman of the Shadow Front, deeply lined kind face, white braids with bone beads, rough wool shawl, a half smile of old wisdom. Warm fire glow, violet twilight.
Marshal Ilja Wolkow called the Bear, sixty-one, broad heavy man, huge gray beard, exhausted calm eyes, sooty worn marshal coat with red armband, hands like iron. Warm red-orange furnace light.

Lieutenant colonel Nastja Petrowa, mid-thirties former radio operator of the Red Alliance, charismatic and sharp-tongued, dark curly hair under a headset, a knowing smirk, red-trimmed olive uniform. Warm red light, bright eyes.

Captain Dmitri called Funke, early thirties pioneer of the Red Alliance, always sooty and cheerful, big laugh, welding goggles pushed up, grease-streaked face, red bandana, work jacket with tools. Warm orange sparks.

Commissar Irina Zeljenko, political officer of the Red Alliance, hard and sincere, severe tight bun, thin lips, red-and-black high-collar uniform with a star pin, cold precise gaze. Harsh red side light.
Colonel Gregor Lasarew, sixty, Red Alliance officer, fatherly friendly smile with cold eyes underneath, silver-grey hair and moustache, immaculate red-trimmed greatcoat. Warm light but cold shadows.
Captain Reyes, energetic coast guard captain of the Westbund, confident wind-burnt face, short curly hair, navy-blue jacket with reflective stripes, headset, spray of sea water. Cool blue daylight.

stills.prompt: Coastal fortress port city Port Meridian at dusk, harbor cranes, cool blue lights switching on, a woman strategist seen from behind at a tall window over a holographic coastline map, long shadows.
Dawn breaking over a defended harbor town, smoke drifting from the hills, exhausted soldiers in pale blue uniforms standing on the sea wall, pink and gold sky, a calm after the night.
A patched-together fighter jet built from three different wrecks climbing at sunrise over the jagged snowy Eisenkamm mountains, long contrails, lonely and beautiful.
Deep in a mountain valley a faint blue glow rises from cavern mouths into the dusk, tiny fleeing villagers with mules on a mountain path below, awe and unease.
Convoy of six heavy trucks with medical and measuring equipment winding up a narrow mountain pass road at golden hour, steep cliffs, a lone sniper sitting on the roof of the fourth truck.
Burning wreckage of a convoy on a mountain pass, thick black smoke, a soldier dragging a scientist into a ditch, a small drone silhouette overhead with a faint blue light.
An army massed on the misty shore of a huge lake in steady rain, a long stone bridge stretching into fog, tanks and soldiers in blue-grey, grim mood.
A lone woman in a hooded cloak standing in the middle of a rain-swept bridge facing a huge army, soldiers slowly lowering their weapons, shafts of light through clouds.
A tiny field hospital of white tents in a dark pine forest at night, warm lantern light, a limping pilot with a bandaged leg being guided by a small boy and an old woman.
Night defence of a forest field hospital, tracer fire in the trees, silhouetted soldiers shielding the wounded, red flares and cold moonlight.
The glass ruin city Aurelia at night, overgrown skyscrapers wrapped in fog and vines, three armies' lights converging from three directions on a glowing dome in the center, epic scale.
Inside a ruined glass dome, a vast crystal prism pulsing with blue light, a lone sniper silhouette on a ledge lowering her rifle, a scientist's hands on a glowing console.
A vast underground chamber filled with a giant glowing blue crystal Prisma, floating light motes, tiny figures at its base, awe and danger.
Quiet dawn over the lake valley with the ruins of Aurelia and a faint blue shimmer over the dome, three small camps sending thin smoke into a clear sky, peace beginning.

A colossal old factory hall interior, two hundred silent machines, one huge old foreman with a gray beard standing before a cold boiler, a young soot-covered apprentice laughing beside him, red-orange light creeping in.
Dawn over the industrial valley Kessel-Ost, tall chimneys smoking again, red banners on the factory roofs, workers and tanks gathered in the yard, warm sunrise.
Night on an abandoned railway line, a rusted radio mast against the stars, a woman radio operator with big headphones listening, a faint pulsing blue-green signal visible in the air.
An old railway station platform at night, tense soldiers around a field radio, the pulse of a mysterious signal shown as soft rings in the sky, conspiratorial mood.
A long column of settler families with carts and children on a high mountain pass, a soot-covered engineer in front, a missile trail streaking from the west across the sunset.
A soot-covered engineer carrying a silent seven-year-old boy out of a collapsed tunnel into early light, rubble and smoke behind them, exhausted survivors, grim hope.
